## Introduction

This study analyzes user integration in semantic AI systems @vohland2021.

Previous research shows [@delgado2023; @capel2023] that participatory design approaches are essential for developing inclusive digital libraries.

As shown in @fricker2007 [p. 15], epistemic justice requires attention to how knowledge is represented and who has authority over meaning-making.

## Methodology

This study adopts a mixed-methods design combining scoping review with content analysis of use cases.

### Analytical Framework

The analysis is structured through a four-dimensional framework:

1. Process-oriented dimension
2. Methodological tools dimension  
3. Participation and engagement dimension
4. Representational gaps and epistemic justice dimension

## Results

Analysis of 22 use cases reveals patterns in user integration approaches.

## Discussion

The findings highlight the need for early co-design in contexts involving cultural heritage or marginalized communities.

## Conclusion

This study contributes a systematic mapping of participatory practices in semantic AI systems for digital libraries.
